The identical reasoning applies to § 99-19-71(4). Two families read one bound record two opposite ways, and the refusal is the one that does not survive the record's own words.
evidence.theA4Point: a packet may never tell a participant it does not state something it does state, and the custody form of that rule is that a packet may not tell a participant no bound record answers a question that a record it binds does answer.
evidence.consequenceForAParticipant: someone on this route is told to go and ask the clerk what filing costs, when the repository holds a $150 statutory figure and its distribution, and is given no figure at all to budget against or to check the clerk's answer with.
evidence.whatTheRepairIsNot: this is not a request to assert $150 as certain. The correct repair is the one ms-fel-set already performs: state the statutory figure and its basis, state the open question the record itself records about justice and municipal courts, and tell the participant to confirm the amount with the clerk.

failedObligations.evidence: The filing instructions page states: 'No committed record this packet binds states a filing fee, or a fee waiver, for this route. The office that answers both is the clerk's office of the Mississippi court that granted nonadjudication…'. The profile it binds carries sourceSections[2], title 'Filing Fee', category 'fees': 'Mississippi Code 99-19-72 sets a $150 filing fee for each petition to expunge an offense under 99-19-71' and 'Expect at least a $150 statutory filing fee for many 99-19-71 petitions, but confirm with the clerk'. The same profile's packetGenerator.feeRules carries the same three lines. And the packet's own petition page tells the participant, quoting that profile, that the operative provision 'appears in both Sec. 99-15-26(5) and Sec. 99-19-71(4)'. Having told the participant the provision is shared with § 99-19-71, the packet cannot then say no bound record states a fee and send them to the clerk: that is the sibling fee trap A4 records, and it is not walked around. The comparison that settles it is inside this same lane: ms-misd-addl-set, built for §§ 9-11-15(3) and 21-23-7(6) where no such overlap is even asserted, devotes an entire block to naming the $150, naming § 99-19-72, and stating why it does not reach — 'THIS PETITION IS NOT BROUGHT UNDER SEC. 99-19-71 … the Sec. 99-19-72 fee does not reach those sections by its terms.' This packet, which has the stronger overlap, names neither section and neither figure. NOTE FOR THE REPAIR: A3 forbids the opposite error just as firmly. The repair is NOT to state that $150 applies to a § 99-15-26(5) petition. It is to name § 99-19-72 and § 99-19-71, state on this route's own terms whether the fee reaches it, and say what the record does and does not settle.

failedObligations.finding: The packet says nothing about service anywhere. It does not state who must be served, does not state that no held source establishes a service rule, and names no authority for that question. failedObligations.evidence: I searched the full delivered text of canonical.pdf and participant-instructions.md for serve, service, notice, district attorney, prosecutor, mail, deliver and copy-to. Every hit is either the word 'prosecuted' in the eligibility phrase 'never formally charged or prosecuted', the participant's own mailing address, or the delivery-of-filing sentence. That sentence — 'Whether a filing fee applies, and how the petition must be delivered ... The office of the court with jurisdiction over the matter is the authority that can answer both' — names two facts, the fee and how the court accepts a filing, which step five confirms by pairing 'how it accepts filings' with 'the right court'. Neither is the service question, and A3's per-fact discipline cuts the same way against a packet as against a repository: an authority named for the delivery-method fact does not answer whether anyone must be served. On the repository side I confirmed nothing is held: the route contract has no service key at all (its keys are jurisdiction, decisionId, ruleId, routeKey, pathwayId, mechanism, statute, stage, outcomeMode, timing, requiredFacts, screeningFactIds, exclusions, packetFamily, packetComponents, notes, and the string 'serv' does not occur in it); there is no packet-set manifest entry for this family; and the only notice rule in the compiled Mississippi profile — 'The petitioner must give 10 days written notice to the district attorney before any hearing' — is cited to law.justia.com section-99-19-71 and is keyed to § 99-19-71, so A3 bars reading it across to § 99-15-59. So this is not an A1 failure to state a held fact. It is the silence limb: nothing held, and nothing said.

failedObligations.finding: THE ROUTE-LEVEL REFUSAL IS CORRECT; A SOURCED SENTENCE INSIDE IT IS FALSE ABOUT THE RECORD IT NAMES. What is right, and should survive the repair: no committed record this packet binds states a filing fee or a fee waiver for § 61-14-9 — this lane searched the compiled West Virginia profile and the route contract and found no fee keyed to 61-14-9 — and the packet names a specific checkable authority, the office of the clerk of the West Virginia circuit court in the county of conviction or juvenile adjudication, in the same breath as the refusal. That is DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 theStandard.met limb three, and the packet's A3 discipline in refusing to import a sibling section's figure is exactly what A3 was written to protect. WHAT IS WRONG: the delivered canonical and boundary bytes, on the filing-instructions page, print 'The compiled profile carries no-fee lines keyed to W. Va. Code Sec. 61-11-25 and a $200 figure keyed to Sec. 61-11-26; this route is Sec. 61-14-9 and is neither of them.' THE COMPILED PROFILE CONTAINS NO $200. A search of src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/WV-west-virginia.json for '$200' returns ZERO hits. What the profile actually records for 61-11-26, in its feeRules and twice more in its fee section, is: 'For 61-11-26 conviction expungement, the circuit clerk charges the same fee as filing a civil action, and a person who receives an expungement order must pay a $100 West Virginia State Police processing fee.' So the sentence is wrong twice over — wrong on the amount ($100, not $200) and wrong on the character of the charge (a civil-action fee plus a $100 processing fee payable on grant, not a flat $200 filing fee). The $200 figure IS held in this repository, but by different records: the route-obligation census and the packet-family build worklist record 'the § 59-1-11(a)(1) civil-action filing fee of $200' for the 61-11-26 families. The packet attributes to the compiled profile a figure the compiled profile does not carry. Under A4's operative rule — a false sentence 'fails under whichever obligation carries the false sentence' — this one is carried by the fee paragraph. The repair is one clause, not the paragraph: correct the attribution, or drop the sibling aside entirely, and leave the § 61-14-9 refusal and its named authority exactly as they stand.

The census pin does not hold at this base. The family's other bound records do: src/lib/legal-authority/routes/single-routes.json rehashes to its declared value at 52,860 B and src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/WY-wyoming.json at 120,012 B, both exactly as source-receipt.json declares. The third bound record, data/rcap-grade-a/route-obligation-census-candidate/route-obligation-candidate.json, is pinned at e615283930c6a9aab3be570ca5dd74a8990deb71dc2817733a3d262e48af6816 / 2,596,466 B and at this base holds e881e8493e694cfcc99f714cbdcfc0424cab8c4a7d22b3e3a9913daab6816ab2 / 2,596,674 B. The receipt's own bindingMethod is 'committed repository records bound by exact SHA-256', and its allSourcesExact:true does not hold. I dated the drift rather than assuming it: the declared hash was the file's content at commit 4fb89c96e, and commit 7613a4b50 ("Montana's MMRTA label named two required documents; split it") moved it. I then compared the two versions entry by entry -- 703 route entries in each, 0 added, 0 removed, exactly 4 changed, and all four are Montana MMRTA units. The WY route entry obligation:runtime-only:WY:human-trafficking-victim-vacatur-w-s-6-2-708 is byte-identical between the pinned version and the file on disk. So no fact this packet reads has moved, and the repair is a re-pin rather than a rebuild. Recorded because it is systemic and not this family's alone: all 31 families in data/rcap-all50/overlays/census-v1 that bind this census carry the same stale pin and the same allSourcesExact:true, and not one carries the current hash.

failedObligations.finding: The packet denies that the repository says anything about the cost of this route, and the record it binds says something about the cost of this route -- by name. participant-instructions.md and the delivered filing-instructions page both read: 'No committed record this packet binds states a filing fee, or a fee waiver, for this route.' The bound compiled profile, src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/WY-wyoming.json, which this family pins by exact SHA-256 and which I rehashed MATCH in this container, carries the row 'Human-trafficking victim vacatur Verify with clerk; statute is a motion route, not a standard expungement filing-fee route' -- twice, at packetGenerator.feeRules[4] and again in sourceSections[9].text, inside a Route/Fee table whose other four rows are keyed to 7-13-1401 ($0), 7-13-1501 ($100), 7-13-1502 ($300) and 14-6-241 ($0). The row is keyed to THIS route by its own label, so A3 does not excuse it: this is not a sibling statute's answer read across, it is this route's own line. What the packet withholds is not an amount -- there is none -- but the reason, and the reason is the participant's best instrument at the counter: told only 'ask the clerk', a participant quoted the $300 felony-expungement fee has nothing to say; told what the profile holds, they can say this is a motion in the existing case and not a standard expungement filing. Under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A2 the compiled state profile is a held source, and under A4's narrow rule a packet may never tell a participant that it does not state something it does state. This is squarely the A2 error pattern the determination names: the claim about the bound FORMS would be fine; the claim about the REPOSITORY is false. The named authority is present and correct, so the participant can still act, and the repair is to publish what the profile holds rather than to find an amount that does not exist.

THE PARTICIPANT'S OWN NAME IS WRITTEN INTO FOUR WIDGETS THAT CANNOT HOLD IT, AT A FONT SIZE 0.01pt ABOVE THE READABLE FLOOR, AND EACH APPEARANCE STREAM CLIPS IT. This is the boundary fixture, whose job is to find exactly this. METHOD: every flattened widget appearance in fixtures/packet-boundary-filled.pdf was decoded from its Form XObject — the /BBox, the clip path, the /Tf size and the hex Tj string — and the required text width was computed with pdf-lib's Helvetica metrics at that widget's own size and compared with that widget's own usable width. The value is the 70-character boundary name 'Alexandrina-Katharine Montgomery-Vandenberg-Oyelaran y Fitzwilliam III', set at 6.01pt, requiring 195.97pt. Every appearance stream carries an explicit clip, 'W n', inset 1pt on each side. FOUR OF THE SIXTEEN WIDGETS WITH TEXT CANNOT TAKE IT: /FlatWidget-7888911063 on page 1, BBox 196.99, usable 194.99, over by 0.98pt; /FlatWidget-2708199956 on page 7 at x=332.887 y=463.385, BBox 187.88, usable 185.88, OVER BY 10.09pt; /FlatWidget-6703682664 on page 7 at x=406.387 y=449.662, BBox 161.12, usable 159.12, OVER BY 36.84pt; /FlatWidget-9668333493 on page 9 at x=124.733 y=493.345, BBox 182.19, usable 180.19, OVER BY 15.78pt. The same string fits in the ten other widgets it is written into, which range from 200.98 to 342.16. WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT THE PERMITTED REFUSAL: docs/RCAP_OREGON_OFFICIAL_PDF_GRADE_A_LANE_C.md protects a value that is REFUSED at the 6pt readable floor and left blank for the participant. This value was not refused. reports/rendered-artifacts.json lists exactly two unfittable refusals on the boundary fixture — cap-COUNTY and Address, both with reason value_exceeds_widget_width_at_minimum_font — and cap-PetitionerFullName is not among them; it was written. THE LIKELY MECHANISM, offered as a lead and not as a finding: production-field-map.json records ONE writeBox for cap-PetitionerFullName, on page 1, rect width 210.08, rectBasis 'acroform_widget_rect_read_from_the_document'. The AcroForm field has fourteen widget kids across ten pages with widths from 161.12 to 342.16. WHAT THE PARTICIPANT SEES: a PDF viewer honours the Form XObject clip, so the name is truncated mid-word on the filed pages rather than printed over neighbouring text. On page 7 the surname is cut off in the line 'Contemporaneous with the filing of this notice, ______ has filed'; on page 9 in the order's own 'Petitioner, ______,'. The canonical fixture is clean: 26 widget appearances, zero exceeding their clip box. RESIDUAL LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY: this is a geometric computation from the appearance streams, not a pixel reading. This lane inspected no raster. The central raster receipt for this family records 0 problems over 30 pages, which is not a contradiction — a clip guarantees no ink lands outside its box, so an ink-outside-the-box check cannot see a value truncated inside one. The two instruments answer different questions and this one answers the question the Lane C rule is about.

failedObligations.finding: THE PACKET TELLS THE PARTICIPANT IT WROTE THEIR MAILING ADDRESS ONTO THE PETITION, AND IT DID NOT. Two participant-facing sentences say it did. The component table: 'the Massachusetts Probation Service Petition to Expunge itself, Rev. 10/11/2018, with your name, date of birth, MAILING ADDRESS and phone written in and every other blank left for you'. And the closing section: 'This is the official Massachusetts Probation Service Petition to Expunge with the FOUR facts the platform holds written into it'. There are three. reports/actual-writes.json reports 3 values in each fixture -- petitioner_name, date_of_birth, phone_number -- and I confirmed the absence on the delivered bytes rather than on the report: extracting page 1 of both fixtures with pdftotext -bbox-layout and reading the band that contains the mailing_address write box (field-map rect x=105 y=484 w=171 h=13, which is y_top 295-308 on a 792pt page), the only words present are the form's own printed captions 'Mailing Address:', 'City:', 'State:', 'Zip:' at x=28.42-100.93, 280.42, 415.42 and 514.42. The 171-point run from x=105 to x=276 is empty in the canonical fixture and empty in the boundary fixture. This is the A4 defect with its sign reversed -- the rule is that a packet may never tell a participant it does not state something it does state, and the harm here is the mirror image and worse in direction: a participant who reads the component table and believes the address is on the form will not transcribe it, and will file a petition with the Probation Service that has no address on it to answer. The substitution is not merely a naming mismatch. The committed packet specification gives the missing component three named static sections and only one survives anywhere in the delivered bytes. 'What the order does' (the seal is irreversible; the record may not be opened even by court order) IS carried, on the filing-instructions page and in participant-instructions.md. 'What it does not reach' is NOT carried in any form: its required text is 'The order is directed at the court record. It does not by itself change records held by other agencies, and it is not a pardon. If you need a criminal-history record corrected as well, that is a separate request to the agency that holds it.' Grepping this route's six delivered pages (canonical 29-34) for its distinguishing terms returns nothing — 'other agencies' 0, 'not a pardon' 0, 'is not a pardon' 0, 'criminal history' 0, 'criminal-history record' 0, 'separate request' 0; the single hit for 'does not reach' on those pages is 'Other charges in the same case, which the subsection does not reach', a different proposition. participant-instructions.md carries none of it either. 'This is not the general sealing chapter' survives only as the half-sentence 'which makes this seal stronger than Chapter 12-60.1 sealing'; its required content — that 12-60.1's three-and-five-year waiting periods, its clear-and-convincing burden and its no-hearing-before-45-days rule do not apply here — is absent from this route's pages. No commercial approval until form status is resolved.

failedObligations.finding: Every mapped write is present in the bytes and carries ink, but three of them are wrong for this route, and they are wrong in the one place on this packet where the printed caption makes the value a legal assertion. On CrRLJ 09.0800 page 1 the printed line reads 'I was convicted of the following cannabis offense(s):' and it governs three anchors mapped to matter.charges[0..2].charge. The canonical and boundary fixtures write into them 'Theft in the Third Degree', 'Malicious Mischief in the Third Degree' and 'Criminal Trespass in the Second Degree'. None of the three is a cannabis offence. That block sits inside the declaration the participant signs under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of Washington. The same three values are then carried onto CrRLJ 09.0870, the proposed order, at paragraph 3, so the order a judge would sign asks the court to vacate theft, malicious mischief and criminal trespass as cannabis convictions. This is route-specific and not a factory-wide fixture convention: the sibling ar-act531-set, a controlled-substance route, writes the route-appropriate 'Possession of a controlled substance' into its own offence blank, and the sibling Washington families write the same three generic offences into CrRLJ 09.0100 under the caption 'the following offense/s', which is generic and which they therefore do not contradict. Only this family's caption names the offence class, and only this family's values contradict it. The field map declares no cannabis constraint on matter.charges[].charge, so nothing in the map prevents the same contradiction at runtime.
